Mena Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Mena's Jewish population made up more than a quarter of the town's 6,277 residents by 1897; rabbis included Itshok-Isaac Lurvin (1902), Shneur-Zalman Ginzburg (1904-06), and Yisroel Medvedev in the 1920s. In 1925, natives of Mena founded two Jewish agricultural collectives in the Kherson region. On October 15, 1941, 124 Jews (per other sources, 31) were shot at this very cemetery, with mass killings continuing through November and December, including 50 Jews killed near a railway bridge and 34 children, five of them Jewish, shot at a nearby monastery. Mena was the birthplace in 1916 of Hava Volovich, a writer, actress, director, and Gulag survivor.
